first member of compound with rāga

items.question: What claim of inseparability holds between the moon and its radiance?
premises: The moon and its radiance are extremely pure.
They have not gone to any separation.
No degree of separation whatsoever applies to them.
items.inference: The moon and its radiance remain utterly inseparable in their pure state.
uncertainties: The compound vidhu-rāga may denote moon and color, passion, or radiance depending on context.
items.plain_english: The moon and its radiance, both extremely pure, have not undergone any separation whatsoever.
